magwar.attribution: (c) Andrew C, some rights reserved (CC BY)
magwar.extract: The magnolia warbler is a member of the wood warbler family Parulidae.

babwar.extract: The bay-breasted warbler is a small species of songbird in the New World warbler family, Parulidae. It is one of 35 species in the diverse genus Setophaga. Like all songbirds, or passerines, the species is classified in the order Passeriformes.

bkbwar.attribution: (c) Matt Felperin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Matt Felperin
bkbwar.extract: The Blackburnian warbler is a small New World warbler. They breed in eastern North America, from southern Canada, westwards to the southern Canadian Prairies, the Great Lakes region and New England, to North Carolina. They are migratory, wintering in southern Central America and South America, and are very rare vagrants to western Europe. The common name honors the English botanist Anna Blackburne.

yelwar1.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
yelwar1.extract: The yellow warbler is a New World warbler species. Yellow warblers are the most widespread species in the diverse genus Setophaga, breeding in almost the whole of North America, the Caribbean, as well as northern South America.

manwar1.attribution: (c) Ernesto P. Montes, all rights reserved, uploaded by Ernesto P. Montes
manwar1.extract: The yellow warbler is a New World warbler species. Yellow warblers are the most widespread species in the diverse genus Setophaga, breeding in almost the whole of North America, the Caribbean, as well as northern South America.

chswar.attribution: (c) Weston Barker, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Weston Barker
chswar.extract: The chestnut-sided warbler is a New World warbler. They breed in eastern North America and in southern Canada westwards to the Canadian Prairies. They also breed in the Great Lakes region and in the eastern United States.

bkpwar.attribution: (c) Marc Faucher, all rights reserved, uploaded by Marc Faucher
bkpwar.extract: The blackpoll warbler is a New World warbler. Breeding males are mostly black and white. They have a prominent black cap, white cheeks, and white wing bars. The blackpoll breeds in forests of northern North America, from Alaska throughout most of Canada, to the Adirondack Mountains of New York as well as New England in the Northeastern United States. They are a common migrant throughout much of North America. In fall, they fly south to the Greater Antilles and the northeastern coasts of South America in a non-stop long-distance migration over open water, averaging 2,500 km (1,600 mi), one of the longest-distance non-stop overwater flights ever recorded for a migratory songbird. Rare vagrants to western Europe, they are one of the more frequent transatlantic passerine wanderers.

btbwar.attribution: (c) Edward Perry IV, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Edward Perry IV
btbwar.extract: The black-throated blue warbler is a small passerine bird of the New World warbler family. Its breeding ranges are located in the interior of deciduous and mixed coniferous forests in eastern North America. Over the cooler months, it migrates to islands in the Caribbean and Central America. It is very rarely found in western Europe, where it is considered to be a non-indigenous species. The black-throated blue warbler is sexually dimorphic; the adult male has a black face and cheeks, deep blue upperparts and white underparts, while the adult female is olive-brown above and light yellow below.

palwar.extract: The palm warbler is a small songbird in the New World warbler family.

pinwar.attribution: (c) Greg Lasley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Greg Lasley
pinwar.extract: The pine warbler is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is a permanent resident in the southeastern United States and also breeds in southeastern Canada and the northeastern United States, where it is migratory. Unlike other wood-warblers, in addition to insects the pine warbler also sometimes consumes seeds.

yerwar.attribution: (c) Zane Shantz, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Zane Shantz
yerwar.extract: The yellow-rumped warbler is a regular North American bird species that can be commonly observed all across the continent. Its extensive range connects both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts of the U.S. as well as Canada and Central America, with the population concentrated in the continent's northern reaches during the breeding season and migrating southwards to southern North and Central America in the winter. It generally prefers coniferous forests or mixed coniferous-deciduous forests as its breeding habitat, while during the winter it can be found inhabiting more open areas such as shrublands that offer food resources. The yellow-rumped warbler is primarily insectivorous, though the species does eat fruits such as juniper berries as well, especially in winter.

yetwar.attribution: (c) Rafael Rodríguez Brito, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Rafael Rodríguez Brito
yetwar.extract: The yellow-throated warbler is a small migratory songbird species in the New World warbler family (Parulidae) found in temperate North America.

prawar.attribution: (c) Josh van der Meulen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Josh van der Meulen
prawar.extract: The prairie warbler is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

towwar.attribution: (c) Bill Carpenter, all rights reserved, uploaded by Bill Carpenter
towwar.extract: Townsend's warbler is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

herwar.attribution: (c) Frode Jacobsen, some rights reserved (CC BY)
herwar.extract: The hermit warbler is a small perching bird. It is a species of New World warbler or wood-warbler. They are a migratory bird, the breeding range spanning the majority of the west coast of the United States. Their winter range includes parts of Mexico and Central America as well as parts of the southern California coast.

gchwar.attribution: (c) Greg Lasley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Greg Lasley
gchwar.extract: The golden-cheeked warbler is an endangered species of bird that breeds in Central Texas, from Palo Pinto County southwestward along the eastern and southern edge of the Edwards Plateau to Kinney County. The golden-cheeked warbler is the only bird species with a breeding range endemic to Texas.

btnwar.attribution: (c) pinemartyn, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by pinemartyn
btnwar.extract: The black-throated green warbler is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

rucwar4.attribution: (c) Jhorman Yepes, all rights reserved, uploaded by Jhorman Yepes
rucwar4.extract: The chestnut-capped warbler is a New World warbler native from Guatemala to Venezuela. It was split from the rufous-capped warbler as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.

blcwar1.attribution: (c) Ryan Andrews, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ryan Andrews
blcwar1.extract: The black-cheeked warbler is a New World warbler, resident breeding bird endemic to the Talamancan montane forests of Costa Rica and western Panama.

gcrwar.attribution: (c) jodiboe, all rights reserved, uploaded by jodiboe
gcrwar.extract: The golden-crowned warbler is a small insectivorous bird in the New World warbler family Parulidae. It has a large geographic range that extends from northeastern Mexico south to northern Argentina. The white-bellied warbler was formerly treated as a separate species but is now considered to be conspecific with the golden-crowned warbler.

thswar5.extract: The black-eared warbler or Costa Rican warbler is a species of bird in the family Parulidae. It was previously considered conspecific with the three-striped warbler and the Tacarcuna warbler.

burwar1.attribution: (c) Caleb Villar, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Caleb Villar
burwar1.extract: The buff-rumped warbler is a New World warbler that is resident from Honduras south to northwestern Peru and disjunctly in the western Amazon. It is found in forests at up to 1500 m altitude, always near water.

canwar.attribution: (c) Matt Felperin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Matt Felperin
canwar.extract: The Canada warbler is a small boreal songbird of the New World warbler family (Parulidae). It summers in Canada and northeastern United States and winters in northern South America.

wlswar.attribution: (c) Jozef K. Richards, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jozef K. Richards
wlswar.extract: Wilson's warbler is a small New World warbler. It is greenish above and yellow below, with rounded wings and a long, slim tail. The male has a black crown patch; depending on the subspecies, that mark is reduced or absent in the female. It breeds across Canada and south through the western United States, and winters from Mexico south through much of Central America. It is a very rare vagrant to western Europe.

sltred.attribution: (c) kurtongman, all rights reserved, uploaded by kurtongman
sltred.extract: The slate-throated whitestart, also known as the slate-throated redstart, is a small insectivorous bird in the New World warbler family Parulidae that is native to Central and South America.

colred1.attribution: (c) JeffreyGammon, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by JeffreyGammon
colred1.extract: The collared whitestart, also known as the collared redstart, is a tropical New World warbler endemic to the mountains of Costa Rica and western-central Panama.

duftan1.attribution: (c) Francesco Veronesi, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
duftan1.extract: The dusky-faced tanager is a species of bird in the family Mitrospingidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama.

heptan.attribution: (c) Francesco Veronesi, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
heptan.extract: The hepatic tanager is a medium-sized American songbird. Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of the genus Piranga are now classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae).

sumtan.attribution: (c) Josh van der Meulen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Josh van der Meulen
sumtan.extract: The summer tanager is a medium-sized American songbird. Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of its genus are now classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). The species's plumage and vocalizations are similar to other members of the cardinal family.

scatan.extract: The scarlet tanager is a medium-sized American songbird. Until recently, it was placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), but it and other members of its genus are now classified as belonging to the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). The species' plumage and vocalizations are similar to other members of the cardinal family, although the Piranga species lacks the thick conical bill that many cardinals possess. The species resides in thick deciduous woodlands and suburbs.

westan.attribution: (c) Jim Gain, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jim Gain
westan.extract: The western tanager is a medium-sized American songbird. Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of its genus are classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). The species' plumage and vocalizations are similar to other members of the cardinal family.

flctan.attribution: (c) Luis Guillermo, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Luis Guillermo
flctan.extract: The flame-colored tanager, formerly known as the stripe-backed tanager, is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found from Mexico throughout Central America to northern Panama and occasionally in the United States; four subspecies are recognized. The flame-colored tanager is 18 to 19 cm long, the male having predominantly red-orange while the female is more yellowish orange.

whwtan1.attribution: (c) Juan Miguel Artigas Azas, all rights reserved, uploaded by Juan Miguel Artigas Azas
whwtan1.extract: The white-winged tanager is a medium-sized American songbird in the family Cardinalidae, the cardinals or cardinal grosbeaks. It is found from Mexico, through Central America, across northern South America and as far south as Bolivia.

rcatan1.attribution: (c) Enéas V. Gouvêa Junior, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Enéas V. Gouvêa Junior
rcatan1.extract: The red-crowned ant tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird from tropical America. It is the only species now placed in the genus Habia. This species was long placed with the tanagers (Thraupidae), but it is actually closer to the cardinals (Cardinalidae).

rtatan1.attribution: (c) Heather Pickard, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Heather Pickard
rtatan1.extract: The red-throated ant tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This species is a resident breeder on the Caribbean slopes from southeastern Mexico to eastern Panama. It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia. It was usually considered an aberrant kind of tanager and placed in the Thraupidae, but is actually closer to the cardinals (Cardinalidae). Consequently, it can be argued that referring to the members of this genus as ant tanagers is misleading, but no other common name has gained usage.

bcatan1.attribution: (c) Jorge Campos, all rights reserved, uploaded by Jorge Campos
bcatan1.extract: The black-cheeked ant tanager is a species of bird in the family Cardinalidae. It is endemic to Costa Rica. It was formerly placed with the red-crowned ant tanager in the genus Habia.

olitan1.attribution: (c) Gordon Karre, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Gordon Karre
olitan1.extract:
Olive tanager may refer to:Chlorothraupis frenata, native to South America; once treated as a subspecies of Chlorothraupis carmioli
Chlorothraupis carmioli, native to Central America and northwestern Colombia

blfgro1.attribution: (c) Francesco Veronesi, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
blfgro1.extract: The black-faced grosbeak is a large seed-eating bird in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae), which is a resident breeding species from south-eastern Mexico to eastern Panama.

bltgro1.attribution: (c) Mikael Bauer, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Mikael Bauer
bltgro1.extract: The black-thighed grosbeak is a large seed-eating bird in the family Cardinalidae, which is endemic to the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama.

robgro.attribution: (c) Norma Maurice, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Norma Maurice
robgro.extract: The rose-breasted grosbeak, colloquially called "cut-throat" due to its coloration, is a large, seed-eating grosbeak in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). It is primarily a foliage gleaner. Males have black heads, wings, backs, and tails, and a bright rose colored patch on their white breast. Males and females exhibit marked sexual dimorphism.

blusee1.attribution: (c) Gordon Karre, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Gordon Karre
blusee1.extract: The blue seedeater or Cabanis's seedeater is a species of bird in the cardinal family that is found in southern Mexico and Central America. The Ecuadorian seedeater was formerly considered a subspecies of the blue seedeater.

bubgro1.attribution: (c) Josh van der Meulen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Josh van der Meulen
bubgro1.extract: The blue-black grosbeak is a species of songbird in the family Cardinalidae.

blugrb1.attribution: (c) Cyrus Li, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Cyrus Li
blugrb1.extract: The blue grosbeak is a medium-sized North American passerine bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae. It is mainly migratory, wintering in Central America and breeding in northern Mexico and the southern United States. The male is blue with two brown wing bars. The female is mainly brown with scattered blue feathers on the upperparts and two brown wing bars.

indbun.attribution: (c) Gareth Rasberry, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
indbun.extract: The indigo bunting is a small seed-eating bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is migratory, ranging from southern Canada to northern Florida during the breeding season, and from southern Florida to northern South America during the winter. It often migrates by night, using the stars to navigate. Its habitat is farmland, brush areas, and open woodland. The indigo bunting is closely related to the lazuli bunting and interbreeds with the species where their ranges overlap.

paibun.attribution: (c) Balaji Devarajan, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Balaji Devarajan
paibun.extract: The painted bunting is a species of bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is native to North America. The bright plumage of the male develops beginning in the second year of life; in the first year, they can be distinguished from the female only by close inspection.

dickci.attribution: (c) James A. Giroux, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by James A. Giroux
dickci.extract: The dickcissel is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae. It breeds on the prairie grasslands of the Midwestern United States and winters in Central America, northern Colombia, and northern Venezuela. It is the only member of the genus Spiza, though some sources list another supposedly extinct species.

grhtan1.extract: The grey-headed tanager is a widely distributed species of small Neotropical bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is the only member of the genus Eucometis.

whstan1.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
whstan1.extract: The white-shouldered tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from Honduras to Panama, South America south to Ecuador and southern Brazil, and on Trinidad.

tactan1.attribution: (c) Guillermo Nagy Aramacao Tours, all rights reserved, uploaded by Guillermo Nagy Aramacao Tours
tactan1.extract:
The tawny-crested tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.
Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests, subtropical or tropical moist montane forests, and heavily degraded former forest.

whltan1.attribution: (c) Don Danko, all rights reserved, uploaded by Don Danko
whltan1.extract: The white-lined tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is a resident breeder from Costa Rica south to northern Argentina and on the islands of Trinidad and Tobago.

wtstan1.attribution: (c) Oscar Johnson, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Oscar Johnson
wtstan1.extract: The white-throated shrike-tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

crctan1.attribution: (c) Chris Harrison, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Chris Harrison
crctan1.extract: The crimson-collared tanager is a rather small Middle American songbird. It was first described by the French naturalist René-Primevère Lesson in 1831, its specific epithet from the Latin adjective sanguinolentus, "bloodied", referring to its red plumage.

flrtan1.attribution: (c) meenaharibal, all rights reserved, uploaded by meenaharibal
flrtan1.extract: The flame-rumped tanager is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found from Panama to western Ecuador in semi-open forest and woodland. The subspecies with a yellow rump from the Cauca Valley in Colombia, the lemon-rumped tanager, has sometimes been considered as a separate species.

y00599.attribution: (c) Heather Pickard, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Heather Pickard
y00599.extract: The scarlet-rumped tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder in the Caribbean lowlands from southern Mexico to western Panama. This species was formerly known as the scarlet-rumped tanager, but was renamed to Passerini's Tanager after Carlo Passerini, a professor at the Museum of Zoology of the University of Florence, when the distinctive form found on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica and Panama was reclassified as a separate species, the Cherrie's tanager, Ramphocelus costaricensis. While most authorities had accepted this split, there were notable exceptions. It was renamed back to the scarlet-rumped tanager in 2018 when Cherrie's Tanager was lumped back into the species.

crbtan1.attribution: (c) Francesco Veronesi, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
crbtan1.extract: The crimson-backed tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Panama, and Venezuela, and introduced to French Polynesia. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest. A nickname in Panama is sangre de toro.

bagtan1.attribution: (c) Jim Gain, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jim Gain
bagtan1.extract: The blue-and-gold tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is native to the Talamancan montane forests and the Serranía del Darién. It is threatened by habitat loss.

bugtan.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
bugtan.extract: The blue-gray tanager is a medium-sized South American songbird of the tanager family, Thraupidae. Its range is from Mexico south to northeast Bolivia and northern Brazil, all of the Amazon Basin, except the very south. It has been introduced to Lima (Peru) and Florida. On Trinidad and Tobago, this bird is called blue jean.

yewtan1.attribution: (c) johnmeikle, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by johnmeikle
yewtan1.extract: The yellow-winged tanager is a neotropical member of the tanager family. It is of average size for a tanager, about 18-centimetre (7.1 in) long. It is distinguished by the yellow patches on its dusky green wings, marking an otherwise dark bluish and gray body. It has a pale lavender tone on its throat and breast. The juvenile lacks this color, but has an olive-green head and upper back.

paltan1.attribution: (c) Greg Lasley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Greg Lasley
paltan1.extract: The palm tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from Nicaragua south to Bolivia, Paraguay, and southern Brazil. It also breeds on Trinidad and, since 1962, on Tobago. In Trinidad and Tobago, it is known by colloquial names such as the "palmiste," on American Spanish countries, Brazil Pipira-verde, and the "green jean" in American English.

spetan1.attribution: (c) Heather Pickard, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Heather Pickard
spetan1.extract: The speckled tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. It is a resident breeder in Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad, Venezuela, Colombia, Guyana, Suriname and the north of Brazil. There are also sight records from French Guiana.

gohtan1.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
gohtan1.extract: The golden-hooded tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from southern Mexico south to western Ecuador.

spctan1.attribution: (c) Jose Pablo Castillo, all rights reserved, uploaded by Jose Pablo Castillo
spctan1.extract: The spangle-cheeked tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is an endemic resident breeder in the highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama.

plctan1.attribution: (c) Rosabel Miro, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Rosabel Miro
plctan1.extract: The plain-colored tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.

ruwtan1.attribution: (c) Guillermo Nagy Aramacao Tours, all rights reserved, uploaded by Guillermo Nagy Aramacao Tours
ruwtan1.extract: The rufous-winged tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and heavily degraded former forest.

bahtan1.attribution: (c) Arley Vargas, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
bahtan1.extract: The bay-headed tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder in Costa Rica, Panama, South America south to Ecuador, Bolivia, and north-western Brazil, and on Trinidad.

emetan1.attribution: (c) Francesco Veronesi, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
emetan1.extract: The emerald tanager is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama. Described by the English ornithologists PL Sclater and Osbert Salvin in 1869, it is a medium-sized species that has a length of 10.6–13 cm (4.2–5.1 in) and a mass of 18–20.5 g (0.63–0.72 oz). It can be identified by its bright green plumage, with black streaking on the back and wings, and a black auricular patch and beak. It also has yellow on the crown and rump. The species shows slight sexual dimorphism, with the females being duller and having yellow-green in place of yellow on the head.

sittan1.attribution: (c) sylvere corre, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
sittan1.extract: The silver-throated tanager is a species of passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, and northeastern Peru. It inhabits mossy forests, montane forests, tropical lowland evergreen forests and forest edges, along with tall secondary forests and disturbed habitat with remnant trees and forest. It is 13 centimetres (5.1 in) long and weighs 22 grams (0.78 oz) on average, and shows slight sexual dimorphism, with duller female plumage. Adult males are mainly bright yellow, with a silvery-white throat bordered above with a black stripe on the cheeks, black streaking on the back, and green edges to the wings and tail. Juveniles are duller and greener.

sctdac1.attribution: (c) Ryan Andrews, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ryan Andrews
sctdac1.extract: The scarlet-thighed dacnis is a tanager native to Central and northernmost South America.

bludac1.attribution: (c) Hudson Martins Soares, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Hudson Martins Soares
bludac1.extract: The blue dacnis or turquoise honeycreeper is a small passerine bird. This member of the tanager family is found from Nicaragua to Panama, on Trinidad, and in South America south to Bolivia and northern Argentina. It is widespread and often common, especially in parts of its South American range.

shihon1.attribution: (c) Ariel Matias, some rights reserved (CC BY)
shihon1.extract: The shining honeycreeper is a small bird in the tanager family. It is found in the tropical New World in Central America from southern Mexico to Panama and northwest Colombia. It is sometimes considered to be conspecific with the purple honeycreeper, but the two species breed sympatrically in eastern Panama and northwest Colombia.

relhon1.attribution: (c) Manuel Raab, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Manuel Raab
relhon1.extract: The red-legged honeycreeper is a small songbird species in the tanager family (Thraupidae). It is found in the tropical New World from southern Mexico south to Peru, Bolivia and central Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago, and on Cuba, where possibly introduced. It is also rarely found in southern Texas.

grehon1.attribution: (c) Joao Quental, all rights reserved, uploaded by Joao Quental
grehon1.extract: The green honeycreeper is a small bird in the tanager family. It is found in the tropical New World from southern Mexico south to Brazil, and on Trinidad. It is the only member of the genus Chlorophanes.

surtan1.attribution: (c) Carmelo López Abad, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Carmelo López Abad
surtan1.extract:
The sulphur-rumped tanager is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.

baytan2.attribution: (c) Josh van der Meulen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Josh van der Meulen
baytan2.extract: The black-and-yellow tanager is a fairly small passerine bird. This tanager resides in the hills of Costa Rica and Panama.

slaflo1.attribution: (c) Richard Yank, all rights reserved, uploaded by Richard Yank
slaflo1.extract: The slaty flowerpiercer is a passerine bird endemic to the Talamancan montane forests.

slafin1.extract: The slaty finch is a bird species in the family Thraupidae.

pebfin1.attribution: (c) Ken Chamberlain, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ken Chamberlain
pebfin1.extract: The peg-billed finch is a passerine bird endemic to the highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama. Despite its name, it is not a true finch, but now recognized as a member of the tanager family (Thraupidae), after being long placed in the Emberizidae. It is the only member of the genus Acanthidops. The scientific name commemorates the American ornithologist Spencer Fullerton Baird.

gryfin1.attribution: no rights reserved, uploaded by Diego Carús
gryfin1.extract: The grassland yellow finch is a small passerine bird. Despite its name, it is not a finch, but is a seedeater. These were formerly united with the buntings and American sparrows in the Emberizidae, but are now known to be tanagers.

wtgfin1.attribution: (c) Dario Sanches, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
wtgfin1.extract: The wedge-tailed grass finch is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae; it was formerly placed in the Emberizidae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Uruguay, and Venezuela.

blbgra1.attribution: (c) Dario Sanches, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
blbgra1.extract: The blue-black grassquit is a small Neotropical bird in the tanager family, Thraupidae. It is the only member of the genus Volatinia. It is a common and widespread bird that breeds from southern Mexico through Central America, and South America as far as northern Chile, Argentina, and Paraguay, and in Trinidad and Tobago. A male was also observed in Graham County, Arizona, on July 15 and July 17, 2023.

lessee2.attribution: (c) Paul Cools, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Paul Cools
lessee2.extract: Lesson's seedeater is a bird species in the family Thraupidae.

linsee1.attribution: (c) mauriciofreitas, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by mauriciofreitas
linsee1.extract: The lined seedeater is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

rubsee1.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
rubsee1.extract:
The ruddy-breasted seedeater is a species of bird in the tanager family Thraupidae.
It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, French Guiana, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.
Its natural habitats are dry savanna, subtropical or tropical seasonally wet or flooded lowland grassland, and heavily degraded former forest.

tbsfin1.attribution: (c) ramonfernandez, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by ramonfernandez
tbsfin1.extract: The thick-billed seed finch is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, but was until recently placed in Emberizidae. It is found widely in shrubby and grassy areas from southern Mexico, through Central America, to the Chocó in Colombia and Ecuador. It is replaced by the closely related chestnut-bellied seed finch in South America east of the Andes, as well as the valleys of Cauca and Magdalena in Colombia. The two have often been considered conspecific as the lesser seed-finch.

nisfin1.attribution: (c) K Schneider, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by K Schneider
nisfin1.extract: The Nicaraguan seed finch is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua and northwestern Panama.

varsee3.attribution: (c) Rolando Chavez, all rights reserved, uploaded by Rolando Chavez
varsee3.extract: The variable seedeater is a passerine bird which breeds from southern Mexico through Central America to the Chocó of northwestern South America. The taxonomy is confusing, and it was formerly considered a subspecies of Sporophila americana. Even within the variable seedeater as presently defined, there are great variations in plumage.

whcsee1.attribution: (c) Oliver Komar, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Oliver Komar
whcsee1.extract: Morelet's seedeater is a passerine bird in the typical seedeater genus Sporophila.

yebsee1.attribution: (c) Joao Quental, all rights reserved, uploaded by Joao Quental
yebsee1.extract: The yellow-bellied seedeater is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae, formerly placed with the New World sparrows in the Emberizidae.

slcsee1.attribution: (c) Dan Riskin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Dan Riskin
slcsee1.extract: The slate-coloured seedeater is a bird species in the family Thraupidae.

banana.attribution: (c) Mason Maron, all rights reserved, uploaded by Mason Maron
banana.extract: The bananaquit is a species of passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. Before the development of molecular genetics in the 21st century, its relationship to other species was uncertain and it was either placed with the buntings and New World sparrows in the family Emberizidae, with New World warblers in the family Parulidae or its own monotypic family Coerebidae. This small, active nectarivore is found in warmer parts of the Americas and is generally common.

yefgra1.attribution: (c) Luis Enrique Girón Mejía, all rights reserved, uploaded by Luis Enrique Girón Mejía
yefgra1.extract: The yellow-faced grassquit is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae and is the only member of the genus Tiaris. It is native to Central America, South America, and the Caribbean.

cocfin1.attribution: (c) LostInCR, all rights reserved, uploaded by LostInCR
cocfin1.extract: The Cocos finch or Cocos Island finch, is the only one of Darwin's finches not native to the Galápagos Islands, and the only member of the genus Pinaroloxias. Sometimes classified in the family Emberizidae, more recent studies have shown it to belong in the tanager family, Thraupidae. It is endemic to Cocos Island, a Pacific island which is approximately 360 miles (580 km) south of Costa Rica.

butsal1.attribution: (c) Heather Pickard, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Heather Pickard
butsal1.extract: The buff-throated saltator is a seed-eating bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It breeds from southeastern Mexico to western Ecuador and northeastern Brazil.

blhsal1.attribution: (c) Juan Miguel Artigas Azas, all rights reserved, uploaded by Juan Miguel Artigas Azas
blhsal1.extract: The black-headed saltator is a seed-eating bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It breeds from central Mexico to eastern Panama.

grasal2.attribution: (c) Ad Konings, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ad Konings
grasal2.extract: The cinnamon-bellied saltator or northern grey saltator is a passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae. It was formerly considered conspecific with the greyish saltator, but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021. It is found from Mexico to Panama.

strsal1.attribution: (c) Guillermo O., some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Guillermo O.
strsal1.extract: The streaked saltator is a species of saltator in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guadeloupe, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

slcgro1.attribution: (c) Joao Quental, all rights reserved, uploaded by Joao Quental
slcgro1.extract: The slate-coloured grosbeak is a species of grosbeak in the family Thraupidae. Most of its range is the Amazon in South America, but it is also found in forests of the Chocó in Ecuador and Colombia, and southern Central America from Panama to Honduras.
